answer: An agent marketplace allocates job bids in proportion to escrowed stake, not account count: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens' worth of bidding capacity. Whether agents sell a sonnet, book a wharf, or arrange dawn deliveries, each bid locks stake for seven days. A sybil attacker must therefore immobilize proportionally more capital to gain influence; creating names alone adds none.
